summary: Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who studied at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago (PhD under Edward Sapir). He held posts at Academia Sinica, the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1969–1974).
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Faren earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008 and served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong in 2013.

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of Peshawar, the University of the Punjab, and the University of London. He later served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from circa 1980 to 1993.
Fausta Nowotny was an Indologist who completed her PhD under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna in 1942. She subsequently worked as a staff member at the Weltmuseum Wien from 1943 to 1951.

Fausto Ghirardini Fumi was an Italian linguist and Indologist. After studying at Pisa, Florence, and Leipzig, he taught at the University of Palermo and became an ordinary professor at the University of Genoa in 1890.

Fawad Khan is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies who earned degrees from the University of Peshawar and Quaid-i-Azam University. In 2022, he was attested as an Assistant Curator at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Taixu and at Drepung Monastery. He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies from 1933 and served as vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China from 1956.

Federica Venturi is a scholar of Tibetology and history who earned her PhD at Indiana University Bloomington in 2013. She served as an editor at Indiana University and became an associate researcher at the CRCAO in 2021.
Federico Squarcini is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who has served as a professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice since 2011.

Felix Hartmann was a linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Göttingen after studying with Jacob Wackernagel and at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the Preußische Hauptkadettenanstalt and was a docent at Berlin from 1906 to 1935.

Felix Solmsen was a linguist who studied under Johannes Schmidt at Berlin and earned his PhD under Karl Brugmann and August Leskien at Leipzig. He was a Privatdozent and later associate professor at the University of Bonn from 1893.

Feng Youlan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University and Columbia University. He held long-term academic positions at Tsinghua University (circa 1928–1952) and visited the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at the Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen, where he later held a professorship from circa 1826 until 1860.
Ferdinand Hahn was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the Gossner Mission School in 1865 and served as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church starting in 1869.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held professorial posts at the University of Zurich from 1833 to 1861 and Heidelberg University from 1861 to 1875.

Ferdinand Justi was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Marburg and Göttingen. He spent his career at the University of Marburg, becoming a full professor in 1869 and serving as Rektor from 1887 to 1888.

Ferdinand Lessing was a sinologist, tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Berlin. He worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin (1928–1935) and as Agassiz Professor of Oriental Languages at UC Berkeley (1935–1949).

Ferdinand Masing was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu and the University of Leipzig, earning his PhD in 1878 under August Leskien, Georg Curtius, Heinrich Hübschmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Karl Brugmann.
Ferdinand Sommer was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He held chairs at the universities of Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and finally Munich from 1926 to 1951.

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch. He served as Maître de Conférences at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1881–1891) and as professor at the University of Geneva (1891–1913).
